description: Borland Turbo C++ 1.0 (May 1990), obtained from Internet Archive's Vintage Software Collection (archive.org/details/borland-turbo-c-plus-plus, 8x 360K floppy images, internal file timestamps 1990-05-04). Matches the embedded runtime string 'Turbo C++ - Copyright 1990 Borland Intl.' found in build/DAVE_unpacked.exe.

source.note: Raw FAT12 floppy images extracted with a from-scratch Python FAT12 reader (no mtools available); disk4/TCC.ZIP, disk5/BIN1.ZIP+BIN2.ZIP, disk6/*.ZIP, disk7/*.ZIP unzipped directly.

candidates.name: Turbo C++ 1.0
candidates.rationale: Embedded copyright string is dated 1990; archive.org item's file timestamps are 1990-05-04, consistent with the 1.0 release (May 1990).

rejected_for_now.name: Turbo C++ 1.01
rejected_for_now.rationale: 1.01 shipped Feb 1991 per public records; the acquired disk set's 1990-05-04 timestamps match 1.0, not 1.01. Revisit only if 1.0 codegen comparisons fail.

rejected_for_now.name: Borland C++ 3.0
rejected_for_now.rationale: Would embed a 'Borland C++' (not 'Turbo C++') runtime string and a later copyright year; does not match build/DAVE_unpacked.exe.

flags_note: Memory model and optimization flags not yet determined empirically; empires_reconstruction (Turbo C 2.0) used '-c -mc -1- -f- -N-' (compact model) as a starting point. Dangerous Dave's memory model is unknown until the first codegen comparison.
missing: TASM.EXE (Turbo Assembler) was not included in this Turbo C++ 1.0 disk set (only TASM2MSG.EXE, a message-file converter utility, was present). Needed once we start promoting MATCHING_ASM regions; not needed for initial MATCHING_C work.
note: toolchain/ (git-ignored) now holds BIN/, LIB/, INCLUDE/ populated directly from the archive.org disk images. tools/setup_toolchain.py's --from/--pin flow can be used to re-verify or re-populate from a fresh copy of the same source later.
